shape.means: edges that bulge slightly, no two alike; living things, people, growth
square corners, a solid base; rules, institutions, structure
chamfered corners and straight cuts; technical, urgent

label.means: a luggage tag tied to the part with a curved string
a tilted double-ruled stamp, inked, no fill
a swallowtail flag on a pole planted at the part

bubble.means: a hand-drawn uneven outline with a soft tail
a rounded speech bubble with a curved tail (the classic)
an inked, cut-cornered bubble with a sharp wedge tail

panel.means: no box at all: a short accent bar above the title, content on the ground
no fill: a double hairline with corner brackets, the title set into the rule
a filled card in the lesson's shape language (the classic)

icon.means: the icon knocked out of a coloured disc (the classic)
a rosette seal, icon knocked out
an open ring with a gap and a bead, icon inside

mark.means: tick or cross knocked out of a disc (the classic)
a ruled box ticked by hand, the mark overflowing it
a tilted double-ringed stamp around the mark

texture.means: diagonal hatching in the shaded band

entrance.means: things pop in with a little overshoot (the classic)
things slide in from the side they relate to
panels unroll top to bottom, labels wipe, bubbles open from the speaker

camera.means: the camera pushes into the part that matters (guidance for the storyboard)
the camera pans along a process or a row (guidance for the storyboard)
